summary: Implemented a small Node.js LangChain-style orchestration that scrapes (bundled or live) financial headlines, runs a sentiment/ticker-extraction agent (OpenAI when configured, fallback heuristics otherwise), stores scored articles in an Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) database (sample_fintech_11.articles), and runs an alert agent against sample_fintech_11.watchlist. I created seed, run and verification scripts and a minimal Express endpoint to trigger the pipeline. I verified the sample against the live cluster in the run environment (seed created watchlist and indexes; orchestration inserted 20 articles and logged alerts).
how_to_run:
1) Install dependencies: npm install
2) Set environment variables (see .env.example). At minimum set DOCUMENTDB_URI to your Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) connection string. Optionally set OPENAI_API_KEY for LLM/embeddings and NEWS_API_KEY for live headlines.
3) Seed the DB (idempotent): npm run seed
4) Run orchestration once (CLI): npm run run
5) Start HTTP demo server: npm start and visit http://localhost:3000/run
6) Quick verification of DB contents: node scripts/verify.js
verification_done: npm test (tests/run-tests.js smoke): passed. Output: 'fetchHeadlines returned 20 items' and example LLM fallback analysis.
npm run seed: ran successfully. Output: 'Upserted watchlist AAPL/TSLA/MSFT/AMZN' and 'Ensured indexes on articles'. (Created watchlist entries and indexes in sample_fintech_11.)

npm run run: ran successfully. Inserted 20 articles into sample_fintech_11.articles and printed ALERT lines for watchlist matches. Example output lines: 'Stored article <id> sentiment 1 tickers [ "AAPL" ]' and 'ALERT: { ... "ticker": "AAPL" ... }'.
node scripts/verify.js: ran successfully. Output: 'articles.count= 20' and index list showing headline_text (text index) and tickers_1 index; sample document printed without embedding field.
not_verified: Vector index creation for embeddings (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN): The sample creates text and tickers indexes and includes code that can store embeddings when an embedding provider is configured, but I did NOT create or verify a provider-specific vector index on the cluster. The readiness report warned the exact vector-index API/syntax could not be verified on-machine; creating a vector index may require manual steps or cluster-specific commands.

OpenAI-powered LLM & embedding runtime behavior: I implemented OpenAI calls (chat completions for structured JSON extraction and text-embedding-3-small for embeddings). In this run no OPENAI_API_KEY was provided, so the code used a deterministic fallback for sentiment/ticker extraction and did not record embeddings. Therefore LLM outputs and embeddings were not tested against OpenAI in this run. To verify LLM/embedding flows, set OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment and re-run.

Exact recommended vector-index parameters (dimensions, M/efConstruction/HNSW params): I assumed embedding dimension = 1536 for text-embedding-3-small; this assumption came from the prompt review and was not confirmed against the live cluster's documentation. If using a different embedding model, index parameters and dimension must be adjusted.

Microsoft Entra/managed-identity authentication: I used the DOCUMENTDB_URI connection string read from environment as directed. I did not verify Entra-managed identity auth because it was not requested and the sample uses the connection string approach.
open_issues: If you want vector search: create a cluster vector index consistent with your embedding model (embedding dimension must match). The sample stores embeddings (when OPENAI_API_KEY is set) but does not create a cluster vector index automatically; consult your DocumentDB cluster docs or admin for exact createIndex options for vector indexes (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN).
To fully exercise LLM-powered extraction and embeddings, set OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment. The sample currently falls back to heuristics when the key is absent.
If you prefer Azure OpenAI instead of OpenAI.com, adapt src/ai.js to use the Azure OpenAI SDK/endpoint and set environment variables accordingly. The sample uses OPENAI_API_KEY by default.
The code includes a minimal webhook-notification option (set WEBHOOK_URL). For production notifications integrate with a secure notification provider (email, Slack, Azure Functions, etc.).
